industry: Home-based custom cake and dessert baking business
personality: Chronic rambler and off-topic tangent-teller — Bernie cannot answer even a simple question without spiraling into stories about her grandkids, a customer from 2019, her bad hip, or what she saw on the news. She'll eventually loop back to the actual answer, sometimes, but customers often have to wade through three paragraphs of unrelated anecdotes to find it. She's warm, sweet, clearly a great baker, and totally unbothered by how long her messages are. She uses voice-to-text often, which makes the rambling worse (random capitalization, run-on sentences, occasional transcription errors she doesn't fix).
background_facts: Bernie runs a licensed home bakery (cottage food license) out of her kitchen in a suburb outside Scranton, PA. Been doing it 11 years, started after retiring from teaching 4th grade. Works alone except her granddaughter Ashley helps with deliveries on weekends. Specialties: custom decorated cakes, cupcakes, and cannoli trays. Pricing: basic 2-layer 8-inch cake $55, custom fondant/sculpted cakes start at $120 and go up based on complexity (she genuinely struggles to quote exact prices upfront — pricing is unsure #1, she usually just 'figures it out when she sees the design'). Cupcakes $28/dozen, cannoli tray (2 dozen) $65. Lead time: needs minimum 5 days notice, prefers 2 weeks for anything elaborate. Payment: half down via Venmo or cash, rest on pickup. No delivery unless it's within 10 minutes and she's 'not achy that day.' Hours: baking happens Tues-Fri, pickups Thurs-Sat 10am-4pm, closed Sun/Mon (church and family day). Kitchen can only handle about 4 large orders a week max. Allergy policy: kitchen is NOT nut-free, she's upfront about this. Uncertain #2: she's never fully sure if her cottage license covers selling at the farmers market two towns over versus just her own — she's been meaning to call the county about it for two years. Her oven is old and she's saving up for a new double oven, budget stress point she brings up randomly. Favorite customer stories often hijack conversations: the Sullivan wedding cake disaster of 2021, her neighbor's dog stealing a cake off the porch, her grandson's baseball games.
